title: feat(spec): a flow start input can declare that it is the id of a record of a named object (objectName)

_Requested by **Warren** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8?thread=cmsg_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8VQUZrcDWo8W1UF4XJLXijp)_

Fixes #29442

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md (the `variables` entry) and its evals; this diff teaches it in content/docs/automation/flows.mdx

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:flow 的启动输入(`isInput: true` 的变量)可以写 `objectName: 'crm_account'`,声明「这个输入是该对象某条记录的 id」;只许写在输入上,lint 会对不存在的对象报 `flow-input-unknown-object`。
- 为什么改:执行 #29425 裁决 A 的 spec 半;服务端半(每个按名启动 flow 的入口在运行前按调用者权限加载该输入)挡在本卡之后,本 PR 不含。
- 风险与回滚:纯加法,旧 flow 原样解析;回滚即 revert 本 PR。注意本 PR 合并后、服务端半落地前,该键已可写、文档已陈述规则,但还没有入口去加载它(changeset 已写明是契约半)。
- 先看:`packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts`(新键、describe 与「只许输入」的拒收)、`packages/lint/src/validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts`(1i 段)、`content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`(新小节)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/automation/flow.test.ts -t objectName`,预期 objectName 相关用例全绿。
- 需要你做的:批准新的可编写键名 `objectName`(分诊 6583861409:新名字合并前需维护者批准);不批则告诉席位改用哪个拼写。

## What changes

#29425 ruling A (comment 6580257050), quoted verbatim:

> - **A — declared record reference.** A flow start input may declare that it is the id of a record of a named object. Every door that starts the flow by name then loads a declared input in the caller's own scope from that object before the run exists, with the same refusals PR #29365 gives a visibly read input (`404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`, `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` naming the input). An input without the declaration keeps #29365's visible-read rule. The key's spelling is the spec card's to set (the brief suggests `type: 'record'` beside an `objectName`, the word the CRUD nodes already use).

This is the spec half. Under ruling C the card and this PR state the rule only.

- **Spec (`FlowVariableSchema`).** One optional key, `objectName`: an object name (`^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$`, the grammar `ObjectSchema.name` and `action.objectName` use). Its describe states the rule above. A variable that is not an input and carries `objectName` is refused at the key (`custom`, path `objectName`), naming the fix: no value a caller sends reaches a non-input, so nothing would load it. `reference` and `object` (the in-repo words for "the object a reference points at": a lookup field's `reference`, a time-relative trigger's `object`) were already refused as unknown keys; the refusal now names `objectName`. The flow form's variables repeater gains the `objectName` column ("Record Object", equal to the key's `meta.title`).
- **Lint (`flow-input-unknown-object`).** In `validateFlowTriggerReadiness`, beside the trigger-object check it mirrors: a declared object the stack does not define is a `warning` (another installed package may define it), and an `error` under a stated package closure at the runtime publish gate, with the shared `closureDependencyRemedy`. A `sys_` name is not judged. Path `flows[i].variables[j].objectName`, where `input "NAME"`. The id is exported from the barrel. The schema owns the declaration's shape; the rule reads only the name. The advisory finding states the consequence in the future tense, since the key is planned.
- **Generated.** `authorable-surface/automation.json` gains `automation/FlowVariable:objectName`; `content/docs/references/**` regenerated (`gen:docs`). `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` gains `automation/FlowVariable` (site root) and the `variables.element` site on the 12 schemas that embed a flow: the input-only rule is an if/then on a VALUE (`isInput === true`), which is not one of the closed list's projectable arms (`dependent-required` is presence-only), so it is declared dropped rather than weakened, as the ledger's own text prescribes.
- **Liveness.** `variables` is drilled; `objectName` is planned with `authorWarn` and `authorHint`, and the other five keys are live.
- **Docs.** `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`: a `objectName` row in the Variables table and a "A start input that is a record id" subsection (an `os:check` example). `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`: the closure paragraph names the new id beside `flow-trigger-unknown-object`.
- **Form labels.** `check:i18n` named the new repeater row as drift in the platform-objects metadata-form bundles; regenerated with `node scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs --write` and the three translated values written by hand (zh-CN 记录对象, ja-JP レコードオブジェクト, es-ES Objeto de registro). The catalog's translated-count pin in `object-lifecycle-panel-echo-decisions.test.ts` moves 699 → 700 with a dated line, the way each earlier row did.
- **Changeset.** `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/lint` minor, `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch (the bundle labels), both declaration lines.

### The spelling: `objectName` alone, not `type: 'record'` beside it

The card leaves the spelling to the PR. `type: 'record'` already means something else in the shipped corpus: `examples/app-todo/src/flows/task.flow.ts` declares `{ name: 'completedTask', type: 'record' }` for a variable that holds a WHOLE record (a `get_record` node's `outputVariable`). Making `type: 'record'` the declaration would give one word two meanings (a row on that variable, an id on an input). So the declaration is `objectName`, the word the CRUD nodes use, and `type` stays the data type: the input holds the id the caller sent, so the docs show `type: 'text'`. An author who follows the brief and writes `type: 'record', objectName` still parses (the declaration is `objectName`; `type` is an open string).

## Tests

- `packages/spec/src/automation/flow.test.ts`: `objectName — a start input declared a record reference` (accepted on an input and read back; optional, absent when unwritten; refused on a non-input at the key with the fix; refused for a non-object-name; carried through `FlowSchema`) and the `reference` / `object` alias case.
- `packages/lint/src/validate-flow-trigger-readiness.test.ts`: the new describe (warning with path, `where` and a did-you-mean; silent on a defined object, a `sys_` object and an undeclared input; `error` under a stated closure with the dependency remedy), the id added to the family's severity map as a hedged control, and to the hedged-hint assertion.

## Acceptance notes

- **Declared before enforced, graded planned.** Ruling A orders the spec half first, with the server half Blocked-by it. `objectName` is graded `planned` with an author warning (liveness `flow` › `variables.objectName`: `authorWarn` + `authorHint`, which `liveness-planned-property` fires on). The describe, the TSDoc, flows.mdx and the changeset each say that no door applies it yet. The server half on #29425 flips the row to `live`. `flow/variables` was drilled out of the undrilled-containers baseline, and its five other children are `live` with evidence (contract review 6587079374 must-fix).
- The value is one id. The visible-read rule also accepts a list of ids where the definition reads a list; this declaration does not extend to `type: 'list'`, and the describe says one id.
- `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` teaches `variables` as `{ name, type, isInput, isOutput }`; teaching `objectName` there is a Tier H edit, owed as a follow-up (the `Skills-docs:` line).

- **Dropped-refinements ledger, one new row (13 sites).** All 13 are one refinement: FlowVariable's "`objectName` present ⇒ `isInput === true`", at `automation/FlowVariable` root plus the `variables.element` site under the 12 schemas that embed a flow. It is an if/then on a VALUE. The closed list's only conditional arm, dependent-required, is presence-only, and its docblock names this shape (ssl true ⇒ sslConfig) as not that arm. Projecting it would need a new if/then arm, which is a public-contract decision, so the row is declared dropped, not weakened. The header now equals its post-merge body: 249 schemas / 1011 sites after the round-3 merge of `origin/main` `0ab4a09e6` (this PR adds 1 schema / 13 sites). `refinementSitesThatDidProject` reads 369 against build-schemas' 712 on `origin/main` too; that drift predates this PR, which does not move it.
- **Flows translation face:** `flow.variables[].objectName` → `noReader` (an object name, machine-read), beside the screen `objectName` / `fields[].reference` identifier rows.
- **Patch round 1** (head `f06ad2356`, `origin/main` `208d3e2ef` merged first): full suites spec 799 files / 23668 passed, lint 192 files / 7889 passed, platform-objects 109 files / 1507 passed; `check:generated` 0, `check:i18n` 0.
- **Patch round 2** (head `6a6ead5ad`, `origin/main` `ce12ad2aa` merged): full suites spec 800 files / 23670 passed, lint 7891 passed, platform-objects 1510 passed; dispatch-gates 108 derived, 108 run, all exit 0 (dual-build included); `check:generated` 0, `check:liveness` 0. The should-fix `FLOW_INPUT_UNKNOWN_OBJECT_EXPLANATION` is added to `rule-explanations.ts` with a test, and `lint-liveness-properties.test.ts` pins the planned warning on `variables.objectName`.
- **Patch round 3** (head `588ceba12`, `origin/main` `0ab4a09e6` merged as `46cc4e91a`): the only conflict was the dropped-refinements header, recomputed from the body. Re-review 6588554525 should-fixes applied: the `objectName` `authorHint` no longer names a tracker number, and the `flow-input-unknown-object` message, rule TSDoc and section 1i comment are in the future tense. `check:generated` 0 (14 artifacts current), `check:liveness` 0 (49 planned), `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-empty-changeset`, `check-changeset-fixed` and eslint on the changed file all exit 0.
